subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown abort active runs and managed exec child processes, or preserve background/yielded exec sessions unless restart or an explicit kill path is used?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve active/background work on normal shutdown, so changing that behavior is a product and operator-safety decision rather than a mechanical bug patch.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Cancel active run and managed exec scopes during normal stop with a bounded wait, while documenting any background process class that maintainers intentionally preserve.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal shutdown from aborting active/background exec work and treat this issue as a diagnostics/docs gap rather than a runtime cancellation change.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines the process-control contract, then reuse that contract for gateway shutdown.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Cancel active run and managed exec scopes during normal stop with a bounded wait, while documenting any background process class that maintainers intentionally preserve.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent process/session surface history and appears in the issue timeline for this shutdown/process-control area.
